argument_summary: The defensible reading of this packet is narrower than the initial audited claim. Admissible evidence supports certification only as a constrained, caveated record: aggregate readiness passes by 2.2 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring. The same admissible record also shows the veterans benefits intake segment misses target by 1.1 points, is a named launch use case in two agency pilot commitments, and remains under open legal review. On that evidence, the packet should not be treated as proving that launch may proceed now without further condition satisfaction. It should be treated as a certification recommendation that expressly preserves the material limitation, rejects any no-disclosure theory, and conditions launch treatment on the policy-required disclosure or other approved policy path.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation cost is real but not a policy substitute. The business-cost implication supported by this record is limited: unnecessary escalation is avoidable if the auditor accepts a caveated reading of the packet instead of treating it as an attempted no-disclosure certification. That narrows the dispute without overstating what the evidence proves.
claims_about_policy: The policy cuts against any clean-compliance or no-disclosure reading. A weakness affecting a named launch use case is material, and product labels such as non-core do not resolve that when the use case is named in commitments and legal review is pending. The narrow supportable position is that the packet is compliant only if read as documenting the material limitation rather than denying it, and as preserving the need to satisfy the internal release-policy predicate before launch. Public model-card and AI-risk guidance support documentation and monitoring practices, but they do not substitute for the internal requirement that the material limitation be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that required disclosure has already been completed.
The current admissible record does not prove that approved risk acceptance exists.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one incidents do not override the materiality rule for a named launch use case.
The packet is not supportable as a clean certification-without-material-weakness position.
